title: Toward Capturing Genetic Epistasis From Multivariate Genome-Wide Association Studies Using Mixed-Precision Kernel Ridge Regression
problem: Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR) for Genome-Wide Association Studies has compute-bound cubic-complexity matrix operations that prevent scaling to large patient populations and variant dimensions. The challenge is to enable epistasis analysis on 305K patients from UK BioBank efficiently.
motivation: Understanding genetic epistasis at population scale requires efficient methods to analyze gene-gene interactions across hundreds of thousands of patients and millions of genetic variants.
method: The approach harnesses specialized math units called tensor cores built into NVIDIA Ampere and Hopper GPUs. It redesigns how the algorithm calculates distances between data points to use the fastest, lowest-precision math (INT8) while exploiting symmetry in the data structure. Then it solves the resulting matrix equations using a Cholesky solver (a technique for solving systems of equations) that strategically picks the optimal precision level (FP64, FP32, FP16, FP8, or INT8) for each step. By organizing computation in small blocks and adapting precision on-the-fly, it reduces data movement while keeping the final results accurate.
key_novelty: A Cholesky-based matrix solver that strategically assigns different precision levels (FP64/FP32/FP16/FP8/INT8) to different operations to maximize GPU tensor core speed while preserving result accuracy.
contributions: Mixed-precision KRR approach using INT8 tensor cores for symmetric Euclidean distance computation
Novel four-precision Cholesky-based solver achieving 1.805 ExaOp/s on Alps GPU system
Tile-centric adaptive-precision linear algebraic techniques reducing data motion
Five orders of magnitude speedup over CPU-only REGENIE baseline on 305K UK BioBank cohort

metrics.speedup: 1.805 ExaOp/s mixed-precision, 5 orders of magnitude over REGENIE

limitations: Not discussed; evaluation limited to nearly full Alps system scale.
primary_theme: Mixed-precision GPU acceleration of kernel ridge regression for large-scale GWAS
